paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The evolution of KV caches in the streaming setting.
model_annotation: The figure illustrates the evolution of KV (Key-Value) caches in a streaming setting, showing two separate plots that track the size of the cache over time, denoted by the variable $ m $, which represents the number of tokens processed. Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled $ m $, which ranges from 0 to $ m_\Theta $, with a linear scale and tick marks at regular intervals, though specific numerical values are not labeled. The top plot shows the evolution of $ r_1 $, the size of the KV cache for the first segment, with the y-axis ranging from 0 to $ c - a $, marked with dashed horizontal lines at 0, $ w $, $ c - a - s $, and $ c - a $. The curve starts at 0, increases linearly to $ c - a $, then drops sharply to $ c - a - s $, and continues in a sawtooth pattern, rising linearly and then dropping by $ s $ at each segment boundary. The bottom plot shows the evolution of $ \text{Size}_{\text{run}} $, the size of the running KV cache, with the y-axis ranging from 0 to $ c $, marked with dashed lines at 0, $ w + a + s $, and $ c $. This curve also starts at 0, increases linearly to $ c $, then drops sharply to $ w + a + s $, and continues in a similar sawtooth pattern, with each peak at $ c $ and each trough at $ w + a + s $. A vertical dashed line at $ m_\Theta $ indicates a point of interest where the behavior of both caches is shown to be synchronized, suggesting a reset or alignment point in the streaming process. Both curves are depicted as solid black lines with sharp angular turns, reflecting discrete updates to the cache size at specific token positions.
